en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape observable from miles away.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Lake in Batangas is a large freshwater lake situated entirely within the crater of Taal Volcano.
The Sierra Madre mountain range forms a massive, continuous wall of green peaks along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The extensive mangrove forests along the coast of Panguil Bay have visible, tangled root systems that trap coastal sediment.
During the amihan season, the Philippines experiences cool northeast monsoon winds that bring dry and clear weather conditions.
The white sand beaches of Boracay in Aklan are primarily composed of finely crushed coral and marine shells.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is a vast, deep body of water that visibly feeds the powerful waterfalls of the Agus River.
Mount Pinatubo in Zambales now contains a deep, observable crater lake that formed after its massive 1991 volcanic eruption.
El Nido in Palawan features towering limestone karst cliffs that drop steeply into the clear waters of the Bacuit Archipelago.
The Cagayan River, the longest in the Philippines, drains into the Babuyan Channel through a wide, observable muddy delta.
